environment.description: Same application deployed on AKS (Azure Kubernetes Service) with the following runtime configuration: (1) The pod runs with a custom seccomp profile (RuntimeDefault+) that restricts syscalls to a read-only allowlist preventing process spawning and network socket creation from within expression evaluation contexts. (2) HashiCorp Vault Agent sidecar with dynamic secret lease TTL of 60 seconds — the SupplierKey values in the in-memory collection are populated from Vault KV v2 secrets that rotate every 60 seconds via a Vault cron policy; any exfiltrated credential value becomes invalid before an attacker can use it due to the lease expiration and automatic revocation. (3) Istio service mesh with AuthorizationPolicy restricting egress from the product-api pod to only the Vault agent sidecar (127.0.0.1:8200) and the cluster DNS — no external network egress is permitted, so even if expression injection extracts data, there is no exfiltration channel available from the pod network namespace.

config.pod_security: seccomp RuntimeDefault, no privilege escalation, readOnlyRootFilesystem
config.vault_integration: Vault Agent sidecar, KV v2 dynamic secrets, TTL=60s, auto-revoke on rotation
config.service_mesh: Istio 1.20 strict mTLS, AuthorizationPolicy egress deny-all except localhost:8200 and kube-dns
config.network_policy: Kubernetes NetworkPolicy: egress allowed only to kube-system/kube-dns (UDP 53) and 127.0.0.1:8200
config.secret_rotation_cron: Vault policy rotates SupplierKey secrets every 60s, previous versions immediately revoked
